description.value: This study examined gray matter volume as a function of cocaine use disorder, MAOA genotype, and lifetime drug use in men with cocaine use disorders and healthy male controls.

spans.text: To examine variations in gray matter volume (GMV) as a function of lifetime drug use and the monoamine oxidase A (MAOA) genotype in men with cocaine use disorders (CUD) and healthy male controls.

value: we predicted a main effect of addiction where CUD will have reductions in GMV as compared to CON.
we hypothesized a gene-by-disease interaction driven mostly by GMV loss in CUD-L.
We hypothesize that a model containing both genetic and chronic drug use variables will better explain the predicted morphological deficits in CUD.

spans.text: Therefore in this study we predicted a main effect of addiction where CUD will have reductions in GMV as compared to CON.

spans.text: In SPM5, GLM 2 X 2 was used for the GM maps, controlling for total brain tissue and age: for the diagnosis main effect (CUD < or > CON) and the genotype main effect (MAOA-L < or > MAOA-H).

value: Individuals with CUD had GMV reductions in the left OFC, right DLPFC, temporal cortex, hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus compared with controls.
These findings demonstrate a distributed pattern of GMV loss in CUD as compared to CON in the OFC, DLPFC, temporal, and hippocampal regions.

spans.text: Controlling for age and total brain tissue, individuals with CUD had GMV reductions in the left OFC [Brodmann Area (BA) 11] (F 1,72 =6.5; P <.003), right DLPFC (BA 9) (F 1,72 =27.5; P <.0001), temporal cortex (BA 37) (F 1,72 =5.3; P <.024), hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus (F 1,72 =8.6; P <.002) as compared with CON (CUD<CON; Table 2 , Figure 1 ).
Comparing CUD-L with CON-L ( Figure 2 , red), revealed robust GMV reductions in the OFC, DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus, similarly to the main effects of addiction.

value: Comparing CUD-L with CON-L revealed robust GMV reductions in the OFC, DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus.

spans.text: Comparing CUD-L with CON-L ( Figure 2 , red), revealed robust GMV reductions in the OFC, DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus, similarly to the main effects of addiction.

Comparing CUD-H with CON-H ( Figure 2 , blue) revealed a diagnosis effect of GMV reductions in the hippocampus; however, this contrast did not produce significant results in any of the other main effect regions including the OFC even at a reduced threshold.

The impact of cocaine addiction on GM was tested by 1) comparing CUD with controls, 2) testing diagnosis-by-MAOA interactions, and 3) correlating GMV with lifetime cocaine, alcohol, and cigarette smoking, and testing their unique contribution to GM beyond other factors.

value: With increasing years of cocaine exposure, there were more volume reductions in the OFC, DLPFC and hippocampus.
The OFC reductions were uniquely driven by lifetime cocaine use, and lifetime cocaine use accounted for unique variance in OFC GMV beyond the other variables.

spans.text: In the CUD group (n=40), with increasing years of cocaine exposure, there were more volume reductions in the OFC (r = −.44, P = .003), DLPFC (r = −.41, P = .008) and hippocampus (r = −.46, P = .003)
Lifetime years of alcohol and cigarette use was evaluated in the whole sample (N=82).
multiple regressions in SPM5 of GMV with years of drug use

value: Increasing lifetime alcohol use was associated with volume reductions across the examined regions.
Lifetime alcohol use was the major contributor to GMV deficits in the DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus, contributing unique variability beyond the MAOA polymorphism and other factors tested.

spans.text: Lifetime alcohol use was the major contributor of GMV deficit in the DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus of CUD contributing unique variability to GMV above and beyond the MAOA polymorphism and any of the other factors tested and more so than cocaine and cigarette smoking.

definition.value: correlating GMV with lifetime cigarette smoking

spans.text: Lifetime years of alcohol and cigarette use was evaluated in the whole sample (N=82).

value: Increasing cigarette smoking was associated with volume reductions across the examined regions, with a significant association reported in the hippocampus.
The detrimental effects of cigarette smoking overlapped with those of cocaine and alcohol in the hippocampus.

spans.text: a similar pattern of results was obtained in the CUD group with lifetime alcohol (all r from −.34 to −.65, P <.001) and with cigarette smoking (all r from −.31 to −.52, P <.0001 )

The MRI parameters of the 3D-MDEFT (3 dimensional modified driven-equilibrium Fourier transform) 39 , 40 sequences were as follows: TE/TR = 7/15 ms, 0.94 × 0.94 × 1.00 mm3 spatial resolution, axial orientation, 256 readout and 192 × 96 phase-encoding steps, within a 16 minutes scan time.
